course.title: Carpentry & Remodeling English
course.summary: Clarify joinery dimensions and details, compare timber and finishes, discuss scope changes, coordinate occupied sites, and hand over specific outstanding items.
course.roles: Carpenters, remodelers, finish carpenters, joinery installers, and carpentry crew leads
course.scope_note: Original fictional language practice, not carpentry instruction, structural assessment, legal advice, or a statement of code or permit requirements. All dimensions, incidents, quotations, products, and schedules in exercises are invented. Structural decisions, hazardous materials, tool use, installation methods, and site safety require qualified people and project-specific procedures. Sources establish occupational context, not endorsement of these cases.

sources.title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics: Carpenters
O*NET OnLine: Carpenters (47-2031.00), U.S. Department of Labor-sponsored occupational profile

modules.title: Confirming openings and measurement references
collocations: verify the opening: confirm which opening and measurement basis are meant
measure between finished faces: state the surfaces that bound a dimension
allow for the jamb: include the frame in the dimensional discussion
establish a datum: agree the reference used for dimensions

case.brief: The hall drawing labels a door opening 900 millimeters. The client assumes this is clear passage width. The note does not say rough or finished opening; no door has been ordered. The designer can clarify the reference.
case.model: The drawing gives 900 millimeters, but it does not identify the measurement surfaces. Do you need that as the clear passage width, or were you referring to the framed opening? I will ask the designer to confirm the datum and jamb allowance before we treat this dimension as an order size.

workshop.title: Ask what the dimension describes
workshop.goal: Distinguish a client's usable-space requirement from a drawing dimension.
workshop.explanation: An opening dimension needs units and reference surfaces. Rough opening, finished opening, door-leaf width, and usable clear passage are different quantities. Even a finished opening measurement may not establish passage with the door and hardware present. Ask which requirement matters before discussing an order size.
frames: Is ___ measured between ___ or ___?
When you say clear width, do you mean ___?
We have the dimension, but still need ___.
workshop.before: The door is nine hundred, so you have nine hundred clear.
workshop.after: The note says 900 millimeters; it does not establish the clear passage width.
workshop.reason: The revision preserves the number while avoiding an unsupported promise about usable space.

questions.prompt:
Client: I need 900 millimeters for a cabinet to pass with the door open. Which dimension matters?
Carpenter: We must confirm the ____; the finished opening alone may not establish it.
feedback: Correct. This is the unobstructed space available with the door in its relevant position.
The rough opening is the framed space, not the unobstructed passage through a completed doorway.
Jamb thickness describes part of the frame, not the remaining usable passage.
Door leaf width describes the door panel, not necessarily the unobstructed passage when open.

questions.prompt:
Designer: What is missing from the dimension?
Carpenter: We need to know ____ measured from.
feedback: Correct. The embedded question uses subject before verb: it is.
Direct-question word order does not follow 'know' here.
The noun phrase 'reference line' must stay together.
'Does' does not form this passive phrase; use 'it is measured'.

workshop.role_b: You are the client. You need the usable passage clarified and have not chosen a door unit.
workshop.challenge: The designer confirms a rough opening, but the client still asks whether a large cabinet will fit. Separate the two measurements.

modules.title: Selecting timber, trim, and visible finishes
collocations: match the existing profile: compare trim shapes, not just overall width
approve a finish sample: accept a particular reference for appearance
follow the grain: describe the visible direction of wood fibers
compare like for like: use the same dimensions and finish conditions

case.brief: For a fictional study remodel, sample A is solid oak trim with pronounced grain and a ten-day quoted lead time. Sample B is oak-veneered trim with a more uniform appearance and a four-day quoted lead time. Both match the requested profile. No sample is selected.
case.model: Both samples match the requested profile. Sample A has more pronounced grain and a quoted ten-day lead time, whereas sample B looks more uniform and is quoted at four days. Those are appearance and supply differences, not a general quality ranking. Which appearance would you like us to use as the reference?

workshop.title: Compare the properties that matter
workshop.goal: Compare two finish choices without treating one feature as an overall verdict.
workshop.explanation: A profile is shape; grain and sheen describe different aspects of appearance. Use the same criteria for both samples. A quoted lead time is supplier information, not a promise about the entire remodeling schedule.
frames: Both samples ___, whereas only ___ .
The difference in appearance is ___ .
The quoted lead time is ___; the site date remains ___.
workshop.after: The quicker option matches the profile but has a more uniform grain appearance.
workshop.reason: The revised comparison names a tradeoff instead of declaring a universal winner.

questions.prompt:
Client: Are the bead and curved edge the same shape on both samples?
Carpenter: Yes, they match the same ____.
feedback: Correct. Profile identifies the cross-sectional shape of the molding.
Grain direction concerns wood fibers rather than the molding's curved shape.
Surface sheen describes reflected appearance rather than the shape of the edge.
Veneer species identifies the wood layer's type rather than the molding's shape.

questions.prompt:
Client: How do the quoted times compare?
Carpenter: A takes ten days, ____ B is quoted at four.
feedback: Correct. 'Whereas' introduces a contrast.
'Therefore' implies that A's timing causes B's timing.
'Because' supplies an unsupported causal relationship.
'Despite' needs a noun phrase or an -ing form here, not a full clause.

workshop.role_b: You are the client. You prefer visible grain but need to understand the supply difference.
workshop.challenge: The supplier revises A's lead time to twelve days. Recompare the options without changing the client's appearance preference.

modules.title: Reading details and resolving drawing conflicts
collocations: check the latest revision: confirm the current drawing issue
raise a drawing query: ask for clarification of a specific conflict
maintain an even reveal: describe a consistent visible spacing
reconcile the detail: obtain one consistent interpretation of conflicting information

case.brief: Cabinet elevation C4 revision B shows a 20-millimeter reveal. Section S2 revision B shows 15 millimeters at the same end panel. Fabrication release is due for review at 14:00. The designer has not clarified which dimension applies.
case.model: Could you clarify the end-panel reveal before our 14:00 fabrication review? Elevation C4 revision B shows 20 millimeters, while section S2 revision B shows 15 at the same location. Please identify the intended dimension and the drawing that needs correction. We will keep this panel out of fabrication release until the conflict is resolved.

workshop.title: Make a drawing question answerable
workshop.goal: Request a specific clarification with references, location, and consequence.
workshop.explanation: A useful query lets the designer find the conflict without guessing. Name both documents and their revisions, describe the same physical location, and ask for the intended relationship. A review deadline is not permission to choose a dimension.
frames: On ___ revision ___, the dimension is ___ .
Could you reconcile ___ with ___?
This affects ___; please confirm ___.
workshop.after: C4 and S2, both revision B, give different reveal dimensions at the end panel.
workshop.reason: The revised statement locates the disagreement and avoids criticizing the whole drawing set.

questions.prompt:
Designer: Is the discrepancy on different issues?
Carpenter: No, ____ show revision B.
feedback: Correct. 'Both drawings show' confirms the two matching revision labels.
'Either drawing' normally takes 'shows' and does not directly state both labels.
'Neither' denies the shared revision and also requires 'shows'.
'Each drawing' requires the singular verb 'shows'.

questions.prompt:
Designer: Is the query about panel size or the intentionally visible strip between finished faces?
Carpenter: The ____ is shown as 20 millimeters on C4 and 15 on S2.
feedback: Correct. Reveal names the intentionally visible strip or setback at this junction.
Scribe allowance is extra material for fitting, not the intended visible strip.
Overall panel width describes the entire panel, not the strip between finished faces.
Edge profile describes the edge shape, not the dimension of the visible strip.

workshop.role_b: You are the designer. Ask for the two drawing references and the affected component.
workshop.challenge: You can answer only at 15:00. Agree how the panel's release status will be described at the 14:00 review.

modules.title: Discussing concealed conditions without guessing
collocations: report visible staining: describe appearance without naming a cause
identify the affected area: locate the observation precisely
separate evidence from inference: distinguish what is seen from what is assumed
request a condition assessment: ask the appropriate specialist to evaluate the finding

case.brief: An existing exposed subfloor has dark staining beside the laundry doorway. The client asks whether the joists are rotten. The carpenter has not assessed structural condition and the joists are not visible. The project lead can arrange a qualified assessment.
case.model: The dark staining is visible on the subfloor beside the laundry doorway. It does not tell me the condition of the joists underneath, which are not visible. I cannot confirm decay or its cause from this observation. I will ask the project lead to arrange an assessment before we discuss any resulting scope change.

workshop.title: Describe a finding and its limits
workshop.goal: Report a concealed-condition concern without diagnosing damage or minimizing it.
workshop.explanation: Location, visibility, and source matter. A stain is an observation; decay and structural adequacy are conclusions requiring appropriate assessment. Keep urgent site concerns within the project's safety arrangements rather than treating this exercise as an inspection procedure.
frames: I can see ___ at ___ .
That does not establish whether ___ .
The assessment needs to address ___ before ___.
workshop.before: The dark patch means the joists are rotten.
workshop.after: There is dark staining on the subfloor; the joist condition has not been assessed.
workshop.reason: The revision avoids turning surface appearance into a structural conclusion.

questions.prompt:
Client: Can you see the joists from here?
Carpenter: No, they remain ____ beneath this area.
feedback: Correct. Concealed means the joists are hidden from this view.
Exposed would mean they are uncovered, contrary to the stated condition.
Fully visible contradicts the limited view described in this case.
Directly observable would claim that the joists can be seen from here.

questions.prompt:
Project lead: What does the stain prove?
Carpenter: It ____ the cause of the discoloration.
feedback: Correct. Appearance alone does not identify cause.
This overstates the information available.
This would claim a cause, and the remaining phrase does not name one meaningfully.
This treats the unknown cause as already identified and makes the sentence circular.

workshop.role_b: You are the client. Ask whether visible staining necessarily means structural decay.
workshop.challenge: The client remembers an old spill. Attribute that recollection without treating it as the confirmed explanation.

modules.title: Separating requested extras from agreed work
collocations: price an addition: obtain a cost for work beyond the current scope
clarify an exclusion: identify what a proposal leaves out
agree the extent of making good: define the surrounding restoration work
review the schedule impact: assess how a change affects timing

case.brief: The agreed bedroom scope includes replacing skirting only. The client requests a built-in bench; decorating is excluded. The carpenter can arrange a separate quotation, but no bench dimensions, price, or completion date are agreed.
case.model: The current bedroom scope covers skirting replacement and excludes decorating. A built-in bench would be an addition. We can keep the present scope or obtain a separate quotation for the bench, including any making good. If you want that comparison, we first need your intended size; its price and timing remain open.

workshop.title: Offer a bounded choice
workshop.goal: Discuss an extra without silently adding it to the existing price.
workshop.explanation: Name the agreed work, the requested addition, and the unanswered cost or timing questions. An allowance is not automatic approval. A request for a quotation does not authorize construction. Skirting is commonly called baseboard in U.S. usage; making good means repairing or restoring disturbed finishes.
frames: The current scope includes ___ and excludes ___ .
We can retain ___ or request a price for ___ .
If you choose ___, we still need to agree ___.
workshop.before: We can fit the bench in.
workshop.after: We can quote the bench separately; its dimensions, price, and timing are not agreed.
workshop.reason: The revised offer promises an assessment rather than unpriced work.

questions.prompt:
Client: Is painting included?
Carpenter: Decorating is listed as an ____ in this proposal.
feedback: Correct. An exclusion identifies omitted work.
An allowance is a budget provision, not an omission.
An addition would extend the scope.
Acceptance records agreement, not omitted work.

questions.prompt:
Client: I haven't confirmed the dimensions yet. What happens if I request the bench?
Carpenter: If you ____ the dimensions, we can request a separate quotation.
feedback: Correct. Present simple introduces this future condition.
The subject 'you' takes 'confirm', not 'confirms'.
The client explicitly says the dimensions have not yet been confirmed.
'Are confirm' is not a valid verb form.

workshop.role_b: You are the client. You want storage in the bench but have not chosen its size.
workshop.challenge: The client adds matching wall paneling. Identify it as another item to assess, not an assumed part of the bench.

modules.title: Coordinating access and other trades
collocations: sequence the trades: agree the order of different crews' activities
confirm room access: establish which area is available and when
protect retained finishes: preserve surfaces that are not being replaced
flag a dependency: identify an activity that relies on another being complete

case.brief: The joinery delivery is confirmed for Tuesday morning. The decorator has not released the study for carpentry access. The hallway is available for a separate trim review at 11:00, but not for material storage. The site coordinator needs the current status.
case.model: Tuesday morning's joinery delivery is confirmed, but study access is still awaiting the decorator's release. The hallway is available for the 11:00 trim review only, not storage. Please confirm the study access window before we sequence the fitting work. I will ask the supplier about delivery flexibility while that dependency remains open.

workshop.title: Update the dependency, not just the date
workshop.goal: Distinguish a confirmed delivery from an available work area.
workshop.explanation: Several schedules can be true at once and still conflict. State the material status, room access status, and resulting dependency separately. Do not use a clear corridor as an assumed storage or work area.
frames: Delivery is confirmed for ___; access remains ___ .
The next activity depends on ___ .
That window covers ___, not ___.
workshop.after: Delivery is confirmed for Tuesday; the study access window is not yet agreed.
workshop.reason: The update identifies the condition that still prevents a reliable fitting sequence.

questions.prompt:
Coordinator: Can fitting start when the delivery arrives?
Carpenter: That depends ____ the study being released.
feedback: Correct. 'Depends on' identifies the condition.
'Depends for' is not the required expression.
'Depends at' does not express a dependency.
'By' could mark a deadline, but not after 'depends' here.

questions.prompt:
Decorator: Is the hallway available for storage?
Carpenter: No, the agreed window covers ____ only.
feedback: Correct. Only the 11:00 trim review is agreed.
Storage is explicitly excluded from this agreed window.
Study fitting has no confirmed access window.
An unloading arrangement was not established.

workshop.role_b: You are the coordinator. Confirm the delivery but ask which area is actually available.
workshop.challenge: The decorator releases the study for Wednesday morning. Discuss what still needs checking with the supplier.

modules.title: Reviewing fit, appearance, and snagging
collocations: check against the sample: compare the specified feature with the agreed reference
identify a proud edge: describe an edge projecting beyond its neighbor
agree a snag description: settle the exact location and observed issue
confirm the review outcome: distinguish accepted work from items still open

case.brief: At a wardrobe review you said all fronts were flush. The client points to drawer D3, whose left edge projects beyond the neighboring front. You have not assessed the cause or remedy. Correct your earlier statement and add the specific observation for follow-up.
case.model: My earlier statement that all the fronts were flush was too broad. At drawer D3, the left edge projects beyond the neighboring front. I will add that observation to the snag list and ask the joinery lead to review it. We have identified the appearance issue, but have not yet agreed its cause or remedy.

workshop.title: Correct the claim and specify the item
workshop.goal: Repair an overstatement while agreeing a precise finish-review description.
workshop.explanation: Use location and relationship rather than a vague judgment such as bad. Acknowledge an inaccurate statement directly. Recording a snag does not by itself identify its cause, the remedy, or the contractual outcome. Snag list and punch list name the same type of follow-up list here.
frames: My earlier statement about ___ was too broad.
At ___, the edge is ___ relative to ___ .
The recorded observation is ___; the remedy remains ___.
workshop.before: You're looking at it from the wrong angle.
workshop.after: I overlooked D3's projecting edge; that specific item needs review.
workshop.reason: The correction addresses the observation instead of dismissing the client's view.

questions.prompt:
Client: This edge projects beyond the adjacent face, rather than sharing its plane.
Carpenter: Then I should not have described those faces as ____.
feedback: Correct. Flush describes adjoining faces aligned in the same plane.
Plumb concerns vertical orientation, which this observation does not establish.
Level concerns horizontal orientation rather than whether adjacent faces share a plane.
Square concerns a right-angle relationship, not whether the faces share a plane.

questions.prompt:
Client: Did you mean every drawer was aligned?
Carpenter: Yes, and my earlier statement ____ too broad.
feedback: Correct. The singular subject 'statement' takes 'was'.
'Were' does not agree with this singular subject in an ordinary factual statement.
Use 'has been' with a singular subject, not 'have been'.
'Being' needs a finite verb to complete this sentence.

workshop.role_b: You are the client. Identify D3's left edge and ask that it remain visible in the snag record.
workshop.challenge: The joinery lead cannot attend until Thursday. Agree the review appointment without promising a same-day remedy.

modules.title: Handing over records and return visits
collocations: hand over the care sheet: provide the correct product-care information
match the product reference: link a document to the item actually supplied
schedule a return visit: agree a later attendance for defined work
close an outstanding item: record completion after the relevant review

case.brief: The owner receives cabinet drawings and the correct finish care sheet. A replacement shelf pin cover is due but not delivered. The joinery lead, Mina, accepts supplier follow-up and will call Friday. The return-visit date is not confirmed; warranty terms remain those in the supplied document.
case.model: Here are the cabinet drawings and the care sheet for the finish actually supplied. The shelf pin cover is still outstanding. Mina has accepted supplier follow-up and will call you Friday with its status; the return-visit date is not yet confirmed. Please keep the supplied warranty document for its specific terms rather than relying on a general verbal promise.

workshop.title: Hand over what is complete and what remains open
workshop.goal: Give the owner usable records and an identifiable follow-up contact.
workshop.explanation: A handover is more useful when each document matches the supplied product and each outstanding item has an owner. A promised update date is not necessarily a delivery or return-visit date. Do not paraphrase warranty terms as guaranteed coverage.
frames: This document covers ___, not ___ .
___ has accepted follow-up for ___ .
The update is due ___; the visit date is ___.
workshop.before: Mina will sort everything out Friday.
workshop.after: Mina will call Friday about the cover; the return visit is not booked yet.
workshop.reason: The revision separates an update commitment from an unconfirmed attendance.

questions.prompt:
Owner: Will the cover be fitted Friday?
Carpenter: Friday is the agreed ____ date, not a confirmed return visit.
feedback: Correct. Mina has agreed to call with status.
Installation on Friday is not established.
The cover's delivery date is unknown.
An update does not establish completion.

questions.prompt:
Owner: Which instructions apply to this finish?
Carpenter: Use the care sheet ____ the product actually supplied.
feedback: Correct. 'For' links the sheet to its intended product.
'During' expresses time, not the product reference.
'Among' concerns membership within a group.
'Toward' expresses direction rather than applicability here.

workshop.role_b: You are the owner. Ask who will follow up and whether Friday is an installation date.
workshop.challenge: The supplier changes the expected delivery. Explain the revised status without interpreting warranty coverage.

jargon.definition: The framed space intended to receive a door or window unit before surrounding finishes are complete.
jargon.group: Confirming openings and measurement references

jargon.definition: The opening measured between specified completed surrounding surfaces; this is not automatically the usable clear passage with a door installed and open.
jargon.group: Confirming openings and measurement references

jargon.definition: A side or top member of a door or window frame.
jargon.group: Confirming openings and measurement references

jargon.definition: An agreed reference point or line from which project dimensions are measured.
jargon.group: Confirming openings and measurement references

jargon.definition: The direction and visible pattern of fibers in wood.
jargon.group: Selecting timber, trim, and visible finishes

jargon.definition: A thin layer of wood bonded to a supporting material to provide a wood surface.
jargon.group: Selecting timber, trim, and visible finishes

jargon.definition: The cross-sectional shape of a molding or trim piece.
jargon.group: Selecting timber, trim, and visible finishes

jargon.definition: A physical example used to compare a proposed surface color, sheen, or texture.
jargon.group: Selecting timber, trim, and visible finishes

jargon.definition: A drawing showing a vertical face of a room, wall, or assembly.
jargon.group: Reading details and resolving drawing conflicts

jargon.definition: A drawing showing a cut-through view of an assembly and its relationships.
jargon.group: Reading details and resolving drawing conflicts

jargon.definition: Extra material specified so a component can be fitted to an adjoining irregular surface.
jargon.group: Reading details and resolving drawing conflicts

jargon.definition: An intentionally visible strip, gap, or setback between adjoining finished components.
jargon.group: Reading details and resolving drawing conflicts

jargon.definition: The supporting floor layer beneath the finished floor covering.
jargon.group: Discussing concealed conditions without guessing

jargon.definition: A horizontal structural member that supports a floor or ceiling.
jargon.group: Discussing concealed conditions without guessing

jargon.definition: Short framing pieces between other members, used for specified support or restraint.
jargon.group: Discussing concealed conditions without guessing

jargon.definition: An existing site condition that was not visible during the initial assessment.
jargon.group: Discussing concealed conditions without guessing

jargon.definition: A project document recording an agreed alteration to the contracted work and its stated effects.
jargon.group: Separating requested extras from agreed work

jargon.definition: An amount included in a project budget for a specified item whose final selection or cost is not yet settled.
jargon.group: Separating requested extras from agreed work

jargon.definition: Work or supply specifically left out of an agreed scope.
jargon.group: Separating requested extras from agreed work

jargon.definition: Repairing or restoring finishes disturbed by building work to the agreed extent and standard; called making good in some regions.
jargon.group: Separating requested extras from agreed work

jargon.definition: A short-term plan showing upcoming site activities and their dependencies.
jargon.group: Coordinating access and other trades

jargon.definition: A point where one trade's work meets or depends on another trade's work.
jargon.group: Coordinating access and other trades

jargon.definition: An agreed period when a crew may enter and use a particular work area.
jargon.group: Coordinating access and other trades

jargon.definition: The agreed arrangements for protecting retained surfaces and occupants during specified work.
jargon.group: Coordinating access and other trades

jargon.definition: Aligned in the same plane as an adjoining surface, without an intended step.
jargon.group: Reviewing fit, appearance, and snagging

jargon.definition: Vertical relative to gravity; distinct from level, which describes a horizontal reference.
jargon.group: Reviewing fit, appearance, and snagging

jargon.definition: A list of observed unfinished or unsatisfactory items requiring agreed follow-up; commonly called a punch list in U.S. usage.
jargon.group: Reviewing fit, appearance, and snagging

jargon.definition: An agreed physical reference against which specified aspects of finished work are compared.
jargon.group: Reviewing fit, appearance, and snagging

jargon.definition: A record intended to describe the work as actually completed, including documented changes.
jargon.group: Handing over records and return visits

jargon.definition: Product-specific information about looking after a finished material or item.
jargon.group: Handing over records and return visits

jargon.definition: A document stating the provider's warranty terms and conditions for identified work or products.
jargon.group: Handing over records and return visits

jargon.definition: A planned later attendance to review or complete identified outstanding work.
jargon.group: Handing over records and return visits

conversations.title: Nine hundred between which faces?
conversations.setting: At the hall doorway, the carpenter and client clarify the fictional 900-millimeter note.
turns: Carpenter
The hall drawing says nine hundred millimeters. Were you expecting that much clear passage?
Client
Yes, our cabinet needs that space, and I thought the number guaranteed it.
Carpenter
The note doesn't say whether it measures the rough opening or finished opening.
Client
I hadn't realized those were different. Does the jamb take up some space?
Carpenter
The frame and open door affect usable passage; we need the selected unit's dimensions.
Client
We haven't chosen the door yet. Can you still clarify the drawing today?
Carpenter
I can ask the designer which surfaces the number refers to before ordering.
Client
Please mention the cabinet, because usable width is the requirement that matters most.
Carpenter
I'll separate your passage requirement from the unresolved drawing dimension in that question.
Client
That helps. Let's leave the order pending until those two things agree.

conversations.title: The floor that is not finished yet
conversations.setting: A carpenter checks a cabinet-height reference with the site coordinator.
turns: Carpenter
Your cabinet sketch gives a height, but which floor surface is the datum?
Site coordinator
The finished floor should be the reference, not the exposed subfloor visible today.
Carpenter
Thanks. The supplier's survey note says existing floor, which could mean something different.
Site coordinator
That survey happened before the floor finish was selected. I see the problem.
Carpenter
Could you confirm the current floor build-up with the designer before fabrication release?
Site coordinator
Yes, and I'll ask them to identify the finished floor reference on the sketch.
Carpenter
Please keep the earlier survey attached so the supplier can see what changed.
Site coordinator
Should I describe the old height as wrong, or simply as needing reconciliation?
Carpenter
Needing reconciliation is more accurate; the two documents may use different reference surfaces.
Site coordinator
I'll request a coordinated dimension, with fabrication release still pending that response.

conversations.title: A width without its units
conversations.setting: A carpenter and supplier resolve an ambiguous shelf enquiry by telephone.
turns: Carpenter
Your quotation lists the alcove shelf as thirty, but it doesn't show units.
Supplier
That's thirty inches of nominal width. Were you reading the number as centimeters?
Carpenter
I was checking because our site measurements are recorded in millimeters throughout this job.
Supplier
Understood. Is your figure the wall opening or the finished shelf length requested?
Carpenter
It's the opening measurement; the shelf size still needs confirmation against the detail.
Supplier
Then I shouldn't simply convert thirty inches and treat that as your order.
Carpenter
Exactly. Please label the quotation dimension and wait for the confirmed fabrication size.
Supplier
I can revise the description now without releasing any material to the workshop.
Carpenter
Please also retain the unit labels when you send the revised quotation over.
Supplier
Done. It will say nominal width in inches, with fabrication dimensions awaiting confirmation.

additional_scenario.title: The alcove narrows at the back
additional_scenario.brief: An alcove survey records front width 1,210 millimeters and rear width 1,190 millimeters. A client calls it a 1,200-millimeter opening. No shelf fabrication size is approved.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: distinguish the two measured locations from the shorthand description.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: you want full-depth shelves and can show the survey sketch.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Is twelve hundred the front measurement, the back measurement, or a rounded description?
additional_scenario.complication: The client says a single average would be simpler for the order.
success_checks: Name both locations and dimensions aloud.
Explain why an average is not a confirmed fabrication size.
Agree who will clarify the shelf detail before ordering.

conversations.title: Choosing the study trim reference
conversations.setting: At a sample review, a carpenter and client compare the two study trim options.
turns: Carpenter
Both samples match your trim profile. Which difference catches your eye in this light?
Client
Sample A has stronger grain. Is sample B a different shape around the edge?
Carpenter
No, the shape matches. B has an oak veneer and a more uniform appearance.
Client
I prefer A's grain, but the room is needed soon. What about delivery?
Carpenter
The supplier quotes ten days for A and four for B at present.
Client
Does choosing B mean the entire study will be finished six days earlier?
Carpenter
Not necessarily. Those figures concern supply; the site schedule also includes other work.
Client
Then keep A as my preferred sample while you check the scheduling effect.
Carpenter
I'll label it preferred, with the timing decision open, rather than as an order.
Client
Yes, show me that effect before we make the final selection for the room.

conversations.title: White is not a complete finish description
conversations.setting: A carpenter and decorator compare a trim sample with an existing painted surface.
turns: Carpenter
The client asked for white trim, but this sample looks glossier than the existing skirting.
Decorator
The color reference matches. The sheen is different, which changes how light reflects.
Carpenter
Could we show both together before calling this a successful finish match today?
Decorator
Certainly. Is the client asking for the same color or the same overall appearance?
Carpenter
Their note says match existing, so I think we need to clarify both.
Decorator
I'll bring a lower-sheen sample with the same color reference for the comparison.
Carpenter
Please identify the sample labels; photographs alone have made the difference hard to judge.
Decorator
Agreed. We can compare them in the room under the same lighting conditions.
Carpenter
Then I'll ask the client to choose a physical reference rather than another vague description.
Decorator
That gives us a specific appearance target without promising every surface will look identical.

conversations.title: The molding is wide enough but different
conversations.setting: A carpenter questions a supplier's proposed replacement molding.
turns: Carpenter
The replacement molding is the right width, but the curve doesn't match our sample.
Supplier
Our stock description lists the same overall dimensions. Which feature differs from yours?
Carpenter
The original has a small bead at the edge; the replacement has a flat edge.
Supplier
I see it now in your reference photo. So width alone isn't the issue.
Carpenter
Correct. This piece sits beside retained trim, so the profile difference will be visible.
Supplier
Would you like another stock sample or a quotation for a matching profile?
Carpenter
Please quote the matching profile first, with its lead time shown separately from price.
Supplier
I can do that. The stock alternative can remain available for the client's comparison.
Carpenter
Label it alternative, please, so nobody mistakes it for an accepted substitution on delivery.
Supplier
I'll update the enquiry to show profile match required, with the alternative clearly identified.

additional_scenario.title: One sample, two directions
additional_scenario.brief: A client approves the color of a veneered cabinet sample but says nothing about grain direction. The elevation shows horizontal grain; the sample was displayed vertically.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: clarify whether approval covers color, direction, or both.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: you like the color but prefer vertical grain and have not discussed a revised elevation.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Does your approval cover the color only, or also the grain direction shown here?
additional_scenario.complication: The client assumes turning the sample also changes the production drawing.
success_checks: Separate sample approval from drawing revision.
State the preferred direction in ordinary words.
Keep production confirmation pending the reconciled elevation.

conversations.title: Two dimensions on revision B
conversations.setting: A carpenter calls the designer before the cabinet fabrication review.
turns: Carpenter
Could you clarify the end-panel reveal before our two o'clock fabrication review today?
Designer
Which drawings disagree? I need their references and revisions to locate the issue.
Carpenter
Elevation C4 shows twenty millimeters; section detail S2 shows fifteen. Both are revision B.
Designer
Are those dimensions at the same end panel, or on opposite cabinet runs?
Carpenter
The same panel beside the study doorway. I've marked that location on both.
Designer
Thank you. I need to reconcile the detail, and I cannot answer before three.
Carpenter
Then I'll keep that panel out of release at the two o'clock review.
Designer
Please distinguish it from the other panels, which aren't part of this query.
Carpenter
I will. Can your reply identify both the intended reveal and the drawing correction?
Designer
Yes. My response will address those points, with the marked references attached for clarity.

conversations.title: Extra width is not an extra shelf
conversations.setting: A carpenter explains a supplier's scribe allowance note to a client.
turns: Carpenter
The supplier's end panel is wider on the schedule than on your finished elevation.
Client
That's what worried me. Will it make the cupboard stick farther into the room?
Carpenter
The schedule includes a scribe allowance, meaning extra material for fitting the adjoining surface.
Client
So the scheduled piece size is not necessarily the finished visible panel width?
Carpenter
Exactly. We still need the detail to confirm how that allowance is represented.
Client
Please ask them, because I don't want the finished cupboard width quietly increased.
Carpenter
I'll ask for separate supplied and finished dimensions on this panel's confirmation drawing.
Client
Can we keep the agreed cabinet face line as the reference in that question?
Carpenter
Yes, I'll name that line explicitly and attach the elevation you already approved.
Client
Then the question is about interpreting the allowance, not approving a larger cupboard today.

conversations.title: A cloud on the drawing
conversations.setting: A carpenter and site coordinator identify the actual extent of a revised drawing.
turns: Carpenter
The latest elevation has a revision cloud around the upper shelves. Did the base change?
Site coordinator
The issue note mentions shelf spacing only, but let's check the revision description together.
Carpenter
Our earlier base detail still appears in the folder beside this new elevation.
Site coordinator
That's possible; not every sheet was reissued. Which base dimension are you concerned about?
Carpenter
The drawer front height. I don't see a changed dimension or a corresponding note.
Site coordinator
Then we shouldn't assume the cloud changes that height merely because it's nearby.
Carpenter
Could you confirm the current sheet list so the workshop uses the right combination?
Site coordinator
Yes. I'll identify the reissued elevation and the retained base detail on the transmittal.
Carpenter
I'll tell the workshop that shelf spacing changed, while base-height clarification remains separate.
Site coordinator
Good. That prevents a partial drawing issue from being interpreted as an entirely new cabinet.

additional_scenario.title: The detail says typical
additional_scenario.brief: A drawing labels a 10-millimeter reveal typical. A separate pantry elevation shows a 6-millimeter reveal. Both are current; neither names an exception.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: ask whether the pantry is an exception.
additional_scenario.role_b: Designer: you can review the pantry relationship but cannot answer from memory.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Does the typical reveal apply at the pantry, or is that elevation a deliberate exception?
additional_scenario.complication: The site manager wants the carpenter to choose the larger dimension for consistency.
success_checks: Cite both details.
Explain that typical does not resolve a stated conflict.
Agree the pantry item remains pending clarification.

conversations.title: A stain is not a joist assessment
conversations.setting: At the laundry doorway, a carpenter answers the client's question about staining.
turns: Carpenter
There's dark staining on the exposed subfloor beside the laundry doorway in this area.
Client
Does that mean the joists underneath are rotten and the whole floor needs replacing?
Carpenter
I can't conclude that. The joists aren't visible, and their condition hasn't been assessed.
Client
We had a washing-machine spill years ago. Could that explain what you're seeing now?
Carpenter
It could be relevant history, but I can't confirm the cause from the stain.
Client
Please include the spill when you speak to the project lead about the assessment.
Carpenter
I will describe it as your recollection, separately from the visible staining we see.
Client
Will that assessment also tell us whether any change to the agreed work is needed?
Carpenter
The assessment can clarify this concealed condition before we discuss a revised carpentry scope.
Client
All right. I'd rather understand the finding than approve replacement based on appearance alone.

conversations.title: The photograph does not show the support
conversations.setting: A carpenter and project lead discuss an incomplete site photograph.
turns: Carpenter
The client's photograph shows the new shelf location, but not what's behind the wall.
Project lead
They're asking whether the existing blocking can support the cabinet at that position.
Carpenter
We don't have a verified record of blocking there, so the photograph cannot answer.
Project lead
Is there an earlier framing record we can request from the original contractor first?
Carpenter
Yes, I'll ask for that record and identify which wall and cabinet position we mean.
Project lead
Please don't describe the missing record as evidence that no blocking exists at all.
Carpenter
Agreed. I'll say the support arrangement remains unverified, rather than absent or inadequate.
Project lead
The client also wants a fixed installation date. What can we tell them today?
Carpenter
We can give the current planning status and explain which assessment the date depends on.
Project lead
I'll handle that conversation and keep the support question separate from our scheduling preference.

conversations.title: A small gap with no agreed tolerance
conversations.setting: A carpenter discusses a reported trim gap with the client's representative.
turns: Carpenter
You noted a gap at the stair trim. Which joint are you referring to?
Client representative
The upper corner beside the landing. I photographed it this morning from the hallway.
Carpenter
Thank you. Do we have an agreed sample or acceptance detail for that joint?
Client representative
There's an approved detail, but I haven't compared the photograph with it yet.
Carpenter
Then let's identify the location and request a comparison before calling it acceptable or defective.
Client representative
The owner asked me whether every gap of that size is always a defect.
Carpenter
I wouldn't give a universal answer. The detail and actual condition matter for this review.
Client representative
I'll send the photograph with the drawing reference, without presenting my impression as a finding.
Carpenter
Please also note the viewing location so the reviewer understands what the image shows.
Client representative
Done. We'll describe it as a reported finish concern pending comparison with the agreed detail.

additional_scenario.title: A ceiling mark reported after delivery
additional_scenario.brief: A homeowner notices a ceiling mark above the hallway-to-study doorway after cabinet delivery through that doorway. No before-photo covers the area. The route is known, but the cause of the mark is not.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: acknowledge the concern and distinguish timing from established cause.
additional_scenario.role_b: Homeowner: you noticed the mark at 16:00 and want it reviewed.
additional_scenario.opening_line: I understand why the timing concerns you; can we identify exactly where the mark is?
additional_scenario.complication: The homeowner asks you to confirm that the delivery crew caused it.
success_checks: Acknowledge the concern without blaming anyone.
State the observation time and missing evidence.
Agree who will review the mark and report back.

conversations.title: The bench is an addition
conversations.setting: A carpenter and bedroom client discuss the requested bench.
turns: Carpenter
The bedroom quotation covers skirting, or baseboard, replacement. The bench would be additional work.
Client
I thought there might be room in the price because it's quite small.
Carpenter
We haven't agreed its dimensions or storage arrangement, so I can't price it yet.
Client
Could you get a separate quotation without changing the skirting work already agreed?
Carpenter
Yes. We also need to clarify making good, because decorating is currently excluded.
Client
I'd like a painted finish, with space underneath for two storage boxes.
Carpenter
Please give us the box dimensions so that requirement is clear in the enquiry.
Client
Does asking for the quotation mean I have committed to buying the bench?
Carpenter
No. A change order would record any agreed alteration after you consider the price and timing.
Client
Then obtain that comparison, and keep the existing bedroom scope unchanged for now.

conversations.title: Painting around the new frame
conversations.setting: A carpenter and homeowner clarify restoration around a replacement frame.
turns: Carpenter
The frame proposal mentions making good locally. What finish were you expecting?
Homeowner
I assumed the whole wall would be repainted so no difference would show.
Carpenter
The quotation doesn't define that extent clearly. Let's clarify it before accepting the scope.
Homeowner
Can you explain the difference between local making good and decorating the wall?
Carpenter
Local work concerns disturbed areas; whole-wall decoration is a broader item to price.
Homeowner
Then I'd like both extents described, because appearance matters more than a vague allowance.
Carpenter
I'll ask the estimator to identify the surfaces and finish standard for each option.
Homeowner
Please include the return beside the doorway; it's easy to overlook from this room.
Carpenter
I'll name it separately so we can see whether each quotation includes it.
Homeowner
Good. We'll decide from those descriptions instead of assuming the word locally covers everything.

conversations.title: A verbal suggestion becomes a request
conversations.setting: A carpenter checks a shelving conversation with a tenant representative.
turns: Carpenter
Yesterday you mentioned another shelf above the desk. Was that a suggestion or request?
Tenant representative
A request for a price, not approval to add it to the order.
Carpenter
Thanks. The workshop heard add a shelf and asked me for fabrication dimensions.
Tenant representative
Please tell them to hold that addition. The facilities manager approves extra costs here.
Carpenter
I'll keep the approved shelving separate and request a price for the additional piece.
Tenant representative
Can the quotation also say whether the extra shelf changes the delivery timing?
Carpenter
Yes, that question belongs in the comparison rather than being assumed unchanged.
Tenant representative
The facilities manager is available Thursday. I can discuss the priced option then.
Carpenter
I'll label it quotation requested, with your review meeting noted as the next decision point.
Tenant representative
That reflects what I intended and avoids the workshop treating a conversation as approval.

additional_scenario.title: Who supplies the handles?
additional_scenario.brief: A wardrobe quotation includes fitting handles but excludes their supply. The client has selected handles online but has not ordered them. The supplier's delivery date is unknown.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: explain supply versus fitting and ask who will arrange delivery.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: you assumed the carpenter would buy the selected handles.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The quote includes fitting the handles; can we confirm who is supplying them?
additional_scenario.complication: The client wants the original completion date confirmed before supplier availability is checked.
success_checks: Distinguish supply from fitting.
Agree who will check the selected product and delivery.
Keep completion timing conditional on confirmed information.

conversations.title: Delivery is ready, the room is not
conversations.setting: A carpenter updates the site coordinator about Tuesday's joinery.
turns: Carpenter
Tuesday's joinery delivery is confirmed, but the decorator hasn't released the study yet.
Site coordinator
Could the crew use the hallway while we sort out access to the study?
Carpenter
The hallway window is for an eleven o'clock trim review, not storage or fitting.
Site coordinator
Thanks for separating those. I'll ask the decorator when the study can be released.
Carpenter
I'll check delivery flexibility with the supplier rather than assume materials can stay elsewhere.
Site coordinator
Please don't cancel the delivery until we know both options and their consequences.
Carpenter
Agreed. I'll ask what's possible and bring the response back before changing anything.
Site coordinator
The decorator has just offered Wednesday morning. Does that resolve the whole sequence?
Carpenter
It resolves the proposed access window, but supplier timing and crew availability still need checking.
Site coordinator
I'll show Wednesday as proposed in the lookahead schedule, with those two dependencies open.

conversations.title: The countertop appointment moves
conversations.setting: A carpenter and kitchen coordinator discuss a revised supplier visit.
turns: Carpenter
The countertop surveyor moved their appointment to Thursday. Does the current cabinet review still work?
Kitchen coordinator
Our cabinet review was Friday, so the surveyor would arrive before that review.
Carpenter
Then we need to reconcile the sequence rather than tell both teams they're confirmed.
Kitchen coordinator
Can your review move to Wednesday afternoon, or is that still unconfirmed?
Carpenter
Wednesday is possible for me, but the client needs to attend the appearance review.
Kitchen coordinator
I'll ask the client about Wednesday and explain why the timing matters for Thursday.
Carpenter
Please distinguish the appearance review from the surveyor's own measurement and acceptance requirements.
Kitchen coordinator
I will. Moving our meeting doesn't automatically mean their survey prerequisites are satisfied.
Carpenter
Once both parties confirm their requirements, we can update the lookahead with real dependencies.
Kitchen coordinator
I'll contact them today and keep Thursday tentative until the sequence is agreed.

conversations.title: The retained floor needs a clear boundary
conversations.setting: A carpenter and homeowner discuss access through an occupied room.
turns: Carpenter
Our agreed route passes through the sitting room. Which furniture will remain in place?
Homeowner
The piano stays, and the desk must remain usable during my afternoon appointments.
Carpenter
Then we need the protection plan and access window to reflect both constraints.
Homeowner
Can your crew simply use the side doorway whenever the front room is busy?
Carpenter
That route wasn't reviewed. I'll ask the site coordinator to assess it before agreeing.
Homeowner
Please explain that I need quiet from one until three, not all afternoon.
Carpenter
I'll state those hours precisely and ask whether the planned sequence can accommodate them.
Homeowner
That sounds workable. Can we have one contact for confirming any daily access changes?
Carpenter
The site coordinator can handle those confirmations; I'll make sure your constraint reaches them.
Homeowner
Thank you. I can plan my appointments around a confirmed window, not an informal guess.

additional_scenario.title: The lift booking belongs to another crew
additional_scenario.brief: A cabinet delivery is proposed for 10:00. The service lift is booked for another trade from 09:30 to 11:00. The building manager can offer 11:30, subject to supplier agreement.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: explain the conflict and propose checking the later slot.
additional_scenario.role_b: Building manager: keep the existing booking and offer 11:30 for confirmation.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Our proposed delivery overlaps the booked lift window; is eleven thirty available for us?
additional_scenario.complication: The supplier can deliver at 11:30 but cannot provide storage before then.
success_checks: Name the conflicting windows.
Avoid claiming the later slot is final before both sides agree.
Confirm the delivery and lift booking together.

conversations.title: I overlooked drawer D3
conversations.setting: A carpenter repairs an inaccurate statement during a wardrobe review.
turns: Carpenter
I said all the fronts were flush, but you've identified an exception at D3.
Client
Yes, the left edge projects beyond the next front when viewed from here.
Carpenter
You're right about that visible relationship. My earlier statement was too broad.
Client
Can we put that exact location on the snag list rather than cabinet alignment?
Carpenter
Certainly. I'll describe D3's left edge projecting beyond the neighboring front for review.
Client
Do you know whether the drawer front needs replacing, or just an adjustment?
Carpenter
I haven't established the cause or remedy. The joinery lead needs to review it.
Client
They offered Thursday morning. Can you confirm that appointment without promising completion that day?
Carpenter
Yes, I'll confirm the review appointment and leave the remedy and completion date open.
Client
Good. That gives us a specific follow-up instead of another general statement about the wardrobe.

conversations.title: Level and plumb are different questions
conversations.setting: A carpenter and client discuss wording in a finish-review note.
turns: Carpenter
Your review note says the tall panel isn't level. Which direction concerns you?
Client
It seems to lean sideways when I compare its edge with the doorway.
Carpenter
For that vertical relationship, plumb is the more precise term than level.
Client
Thanks. I wasn't sure how to describe the leaning without using the wrong word.
Carpenter
We can say the vertical edge appears out of plumb and request a check.
Client
Does appears mean you're dismissing what I can see from the hall?
Carpenter
No. It preserves your observation while distinguishing it from a completed measurement or assessment.
Client
Then include my viewing position so the joinery lead can examine the same concern.
Carpenter
I will. The review should address that panel, not every cabinet in the room.
Client
That is the item I meant; the revised wording makes the concern much clearer.

conversations.title: The agreed sample covers sheen
conversations.setting: A carpenter and owner compare a finished panel with an acceptance sample.
turns: Carpenter
The acceptance sample records sheen and color. Which feature differs on this installed panel?
Owner
The sheen looks similar, but there's a grain patch I don't like near the handle.
Carpenter
That is a separate appearance concern. The sample note doesn't establish a grain-pattern guarantee.
Owner
I understand wood varies, but I'd still like someone to review the visible patch.
Carpenter
Of course. I'll record its location and your concern without saying the sample settles it.
Owner
Please don't mark the whole panel accepted just because the sheen matches our reference.
Carpenter
I'll keep the grain concern open and distinguish it from the matched sheen.
Owner
Could the supplier show what variation was described when we selected this material?
Carpenter
Yes, I'll request that information for the review, alongside the panel and sample references.
Owner
Then we can discuss the specific concern with the right information rather than argue over match.

additional_scenario.title: An item is done but not checked
additional_scenario.brief: A snag list, also called a punch list, has five trim items. Items 1 and 2, the hall baseboard and study casing, are completed and reviewed. Items 3 and 4, the pantry return and window joint, are reported complete but not client-reviewed. Item 5, the store-door molding, awaits replacement.
additional_scenario.role_a: Carpenter: separate completed work, reviewed items, and the pending replacement.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: you can review items 3 and 4, the pantry return and window joint, at 15:00.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Four items are reported complete, but you have reviewed only two so far.
additional_scenario.complication: The client suggests marking all five closed before the afternoon visit.
success_checks: Give the three different statuses.
Confirm which two items will be reviewed at 15:00.
Keep the replacement item open.

conversations.title: Friday is the call, not the visit
conversations.setting: A carpenter hands over cabinet documents to the owner.
turns: Carpenter
Here are the cabinet drawings and the care sheet for the finish actually supplied.
Owner
Thank you. The shelf pin cover is missing; is that still on your list?
Carpenter
Yes, it remains outstanding. Mina has accepted supplier follow-up and will call you Friday.
Owner
Does that mean someone will arrive Friday to fit the cover in the cabinet?
Carpenter
No, Friday is the update date. The cover hasn't arrived, so attendance isn't confirmed.
Owner
Please make that distinction clear; I need notice before taking time off work.
Carpenter
I'll record your need for notice and ask Mina to agree any visit directly.
Owner
Can you also explain whether the warranty covers every mark on the finish?
Carpenter
The supplied document states its terms. I shouldn't replace those with a broad verbal promise.
Owner
Understood. I'll keep it with the care sheet and expect Mina's status call Friday.

conversations.title: The manual belongs to the old hardware
conversations.setting: A carpenter and client identify a mismatched handover leaflet.
turns: Carpenter
You've found a different hinge model on the leaflet. Let's compare the product references.
Client
The installed hardware was changed during procurement, but this leaflet shows the first selection.
Carpenter
Then the handover pack needs correction. Please keep this copy separate from the applicable information.
Client
Can you obtain the correct document without asking me to identify the replacement myself?
Carpenter
Yes. I'll use the recorded supply reference and request the matching leaflet from the supplier.
Client
I'd like the as-built record to show that hardware substitution accurately for future enquiries.
Carpenter
I'll ask the joinery lead to reconcile the record with the confirmed supplied product.
Client
Will you send a complete corrected pack or only the new individual page?
Carpenter
A complete identified pack will be clearer, with the superseded document noted in the covering message.
Client
Good. I can then keep one reliable set instead of guessing which loose sheet applies.

conversations.title: A callback needs a specific description
conversations.setting: A carpenter clarifies a client's request for a return visit.
turns: Carpenter
Your message asks us to come back about the cupboard. What has changed?
Client
The upper left door rubs the neighboring front when I open it now.
Carpenter
When did you first notice that, and is this the cupboard beside the window?
Client
Yesterday evening, and yes, the window cupboard. The other doors seem unchanged to me.
Carpenter
I'll record that description and arrange a review rather than suggest an adjustment by phone.
Client
Thank you. I don't want to alter the hardware myself and complicate the review.
Carpenter
The service coordinator can offer appointment windows. May they contact you on this number?
Client
Yes, afternoons are easiest, except Wednesday when the room is being used for meetings.
Carpenter
I'll pass on those availability limits and keep the item identified as a reported concern.
Client
Please do. A defined review appointment will help more than a promise to drop by sometime.

additional_scenario.title: The named contact is away
additional_scenario.brief: The owner expects a Friday update about replacement drawer front D6. Its delivery date is unconfirmed. Mina is away; colleague Joel can accept supplier follow-up but has not yet spoken to the supplier.
additional_scenario.role_a: Outgoing carpenter: ask Joel to accept the follow-up and distinguish known status from an expected reply.
additional_scenario.role_b: Joel: you can contact the supplier today and call the owner Friday regardless of whether a date is confirmed.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Can you take over the drawer-front follow-up while Mina is away?
additional_scenario.complication: The owner asks whether the change of contact means the part has arrived.
success_checks: Confirm Joel accepts the task.
Preserve the unknown delivery status.
Keep Friday as an update, not a delivery promise.

dialogues.title: The survey note and the door schedule
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and designer reconcile references for a utility-room door without selecting an installation method.
dialogue: Carpenter
The utility door schedule shows a unit width, while the survey labels an opening. Can we reconcile them?
Designer
Yes. Which drawing revision and survey location are you using for that comparison this morning?
Carpenter
Revision C, doorway U2. The survey was taken before the wall finishes were added on either side.
Designer
Then the survey dimension describes an earlier condition. The schedule refers to the proposed door unit itself.
Carpenter
The client has asked for the usable passage width, so neither number answers that question directly.
Designer
Correct. We need the completed opening relationship, including the selected frame, before confirming usable width to them.
Carpenter
Could you issue a marked detail identifying the datum and the surfaces for each dimension?
Designer
I can prepare that clarification. Please keep the supplier's order on hold while I reconcile the documents.
Carpenter
I will. Should I tell the client the proposed door is unsuitable for their delivery trolley?
Designer
Not yet; suitability hasn't been established either way. Ask for the trolley's actual dimensions and turning requirements.
Carpenter
They can provide those today. I'll identify them as client requirements, not alter your drawing myself.
Designer
Good. Send them with the survey, and we'll answer the passage question against one coordinated detail.
notes: 'Neither number answers that question' separates two valid measurements from the client's different requirement.
'Hasn't been established either way' avoids turning uncertainty into a rejection.

dialogues.title: Matching old oak without promising an exact twin
dialogues.setting: A remodeling carpenter and homeowner discuss new shelving beside existing oak paneling.
dialogue: Carpenter
The new oak sample is close in color, but its grain differs from the paneling you are retaining.
Homeowner
I noticed that. Can the supplier guarantee an exact match if we choose a more expensive board?
Carpenter
Price alone wouldn't establish that. Wood varies, and the existing finish has its own age and appearance.
Homeowner
I mainly want the shelves to look intentional, rather than like a failed attempt at matching.
Carpenter
Then we can compare a close match with a deliberate contrast, using actual samples beside the paneling.
Homeowner
Would a contrasting finish mean changing the shelf profile as well, or only the visible surface?
Carpenter
Only the surface in these options. Both examples retain the agreed square edge and the same dimensions.
Homeowner
The darker sample looks deliberate. I would like to see it under our evening lighting before deciding.
Carpenter
I'll leave the labeled sample here and keep the material selection open until tomorrow.
Homeowner
Please make sure the workshop doesn't treat our discussion as approval to start making the shelves.
Carpenter
I'll tell them color review is pending. The profile remains agreed, but the finish is not selected.
Homeowner
Thank you. Tomorrow I'll choose between these two references, rather than asking for an impossible identical grain.
notes: 'A deliberate contrast' offers a positive alternative to a poorly defined exact match.
'The profile remains agreed' preserves a settled decision while isolating the open finish choice.

dialogues.title: An old detail inside a new email
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and cabinet supplier discover that an attachment does not match its covering email.
dialogue: Carpenter
Your email says revised for approval, but the attached section still has the original drawer-front arrangement.
Supplier
That's unexpected. Are you comparing the attachment with the elevation we discussed during yesterday's review meeting?
Carpenter
Yes. The elevation shows two equal fronts; this section still labels three different front heights.
Supplier
I may have attached the earlier file. Please tell me the revision letter printed on its border.
Carpenter
It says A, while your email refers to C. I haven't released the cabinet to fabrication.
Supplier
Thank you for catching that. I'll resend the correct section and identify the superseded attachment clearly.
Carpenter
Please include the matching elevation too, so the workshop receives one coordinated set rather than isolated sheets.
Supplier
I can issue those together. Does the client need to reconsider the finish sample as part of this?
Carpenter
No, the finish hasn't changed. This query concerns the drawer arrangement and the documents describing it.
Supplier
Understood. I'll keep the finish approval reference and show the drawing correction as a separate change.
Carpenter
Once I receive the set, I'll compare the section and elevation before confirming its review status.
Supplier
That works. The earlier email remains a record of transmission, not evidence that the incorrect attachment was approved.
notes: 'Superseded attachment' identifies a replaced document without pretending it was never sent.
'This query concerns' narrows a correction so unrelated approvals do not become uncertain.

dialogues.title: A wall that may not be straight
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and homeowner discuss uneven visible spacing beside a proposed built-in unit.
dialogue: Carpenter
The survey shows different widths at the front and rear of this alcove.
Homeowner
Does that mean the wall is unsound? The old bookcase always looked slightly crooked here.
Carpenter
Different widths alone don't establish structural condition. They tell us the space is not uniform at those points.
Homeowner
I see. My main concern is the cabinet looking straight when we view it from the doorway.
Carpenter
That's an appearance requirement we can discuss. The drawing needs to show the face line and adjoining relationship.
Homeowner
Can you promise the visible gap will disappear completely once the cabinet is fitted into the alcove?
Carpenter
Not without an agreed detail. A scribed panel might be considered, but design review comes first.
Homeowner
Then please ask for a detail that shows what remains visible, not just the overall cabinet width.
Carpenter
I'll do that and include the actual survey points so the designer has the same information.
Homeowner
Will the new detail mean another charge, or is it part of the existing cabinet proposal?
Carpenter
The project manager needs to clarify that scope question. I can describe the issue, not decide the commercial terms.
Homeowner
Please arrange both clarifications together. I'll hold my appearance approval until I can see the proposed finished relationship.
notes: 'Different widths alone' limits the inference to the actual measurement evidence.
'That's an appearance requirement' acknowledges the client's priority without substituting it for a structural assessment.

dialogues.title: One extra room, two possible packages
dialogues.setting: A remodeling carpenter and owner discuss extending a trim package to a second room.
dialogue: Carpenter
You asked about adding the dining room. The current package covers the sitting room only.
Owner
Yes. I'd like matching trim in both, but I need a useful comparison before deciding.
Carpenter
We can quote the dining room separately or request a combined revision covering both rooms.
Owner
Would the combined revision automatically include repainting the doors as well as the new trim?
Carpenter
No. We should list door painting explicitly if you want it included in that comparison.
Owner
Please include it as a separate line. I might keep the existing door finish after all.
Carpenter
I'll distinguish trim supply, fitting, and the requested decorating extent, with timing for each proposed package.
Owner
The estimate has an allowance. Doesn't that mean the extra room is already partly paid for?
Carpenter
That allowance is identified for the sitting-room trim selection, not an unspecified amount of extra work.
Owner
Understood. Keep that reference visible so I can compare the original scope with the proposed addition.
Carpenter
I will ask for the difference to be shown clearly, without treating either proposal as accepted.
Owner
Then I'll review both packages with the decorator before approving any extension of the work.
notes: 'As a separate line' requests a visible scope distinction within a quotation.
'Not an unspecified amount of extra work' clarifies an allowance without interpreting contractual rights.

dialogues.title: A handover between the floor and cabinet teams
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and flooring supervisor settle the boundaries of an upcoming room release.
dialogue: Carpenter
The lookahead says kitchen available Friday. Does that mean your work and room release are both complete?
Flooring supervisor
Our floor installation is planned to finish Friday, but the room-release conditions still need confirmation.
Carpenter
Thanks. The phrase available sounded broader than that when the cabinet supplier read the schedule yesterday.
Flooring supervisor
I understand. We should replace it with a clear status, including what remains to be checked.
Carpenter
Can you give the coordinator that distinction today? The delivery booking needs a decision tomorrow morning.
Flooring supervisor
Yes. I'll report installation timing separately from access release and name the person confirming the latter.
Carpenter
The supplier also asks whether their delivery route crosses the retained hallway finish beside the kitchen.
Flooring supervisor
It does. That interface belongs in the protection discussion, rather than being left to the delivery crew.
Carpenter
I'll include it in the coordination call, with the agreed hallway restrictions visible to everyone attending.
Flooring supervisor
Good. Please avoid telling the client the cabinets are delayed by flooring before the options are reviewed.
Carpenter
Agreed. Let's confirm access and check the delivery options before saying the flooring team has delayed us.
Flooring supervisor
Then our update will identify the open release condition and tomorrow's booking decision without assigning unsupported blame.
notes: 'The phrase ... sounded broader' repairs an interpretation without accusing the other trade.
'Separately from access release' distinguishes finishing an activity from authorizing the next crew's access.

dialogues.title: A finish concern after the review meeting
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and client agree how to handle a new snag reported after an earlier walkthrough.
dialogue: Carpenter
You sent a photograph after yesterday's walkthrough. Which feature would you like reviewed?
Client
The joint above the left corner looks uneven in daylight, although I didn't notice it last evening.
Carpenter
Thank you. I'll identify that joint and the lighting difference rather than say the entire trim failed.
Client
Will raising it now cancel the other items we agreed were satisfactory during the walkthrough?
Carpenter
Not automatically in our review record. We can keep those observations and add this specific concern separately.
Client
I'd like that. The rest of the room looks good, and I don't want the issue exaggerated.
Carpenter
Do you have the original image available? The messaging app preview makes the corner hard to see.
Client
Yes, I'll send the full image and indicate the left corner on a second copy for orientation.
Carpenter
I'll ask the joinery lead to review it against the detail, with the cause and remedy still open.
Client
Please include me in the appointment. I want to show the exact view before anything is proposed.
Carpenter
Thursday at ten is available for that review. Is that suitable for you to attend in person?
Client
Yes. Confirm Thursday's review, and describe it as the window-joint concern rather than a complete room rejection.
notes: 'Add this specific concern separately' preserves earlier decisions while allowing new evidence.
'For orientation' explains why a marked copy accompanies the original photograph.

dialogues.title: The owner needs a useful final record
dialogues.setting: A carpenter and facilities representative review a remodeled meeting room's handover pack.
dialogue: Carpenter
The pack contains cabinet records, finish references, and supplier documents. One trim item remains open.
Facilities representative
Which item? I need to explain the room status to our incoming colleague.
Carpenter
The short molding beside the store door is awaiting replacement. Everything else on this list has been reviewed.
Facilities representative
Please keep review status separate from warranty terms; our incoming colleague sometimes confuses them.
Carpenter
I will. The warranty document is separate, and any coverage question should refer to its actual terms.
Facilities representative
Is the molding's return visit booked, or are we still waiting for the supplier to confirm availability?
Carpenter
Availability is still pending. Joel owns the follow-up and has agreed to update you on Monday afternoon.
Facilities representative
Can the incoming colleague be included, so the handover doesn't depend on forwarding my messages later?
Carpenter
Yes. With your agreed contact details, I'll include them and ask them to acknowledge receipt of the pack.
Facilities representative
Their name is Lena. I'll introduce her today and explain that the molding remains an open item.
Carpenter
Then Monday's update will go to both of you, without presenting the room record as a completion guarantee.
Facilities representative
Lena will have the documents, the open item, and a named contact to follow up with.
notes: 'Availability is still pending' distinguishes procurement status from an appointment booking.
'Acknowledge receipt' checks delivery of the information without treating receipt as technical acceptance.
